response.strategyText: Terry enters this first Cerulean encounter with a tightly bound, source-authored roster of four Pokémon, each carrying a distinct tactical role. His signature Charmander (Level 18) is the centerpiece—confident, aggressive, and emotionally anchored to him—bearing moves like Metal Claw, Uproar, and stat-shifting effects that suggest a setup-heavy, momentum-driven fighter. Pidgeotto (17) and Rattata (15) offer quick physical pressure and utility (Nightmare, Quick Attack), while Abra (16) sits as a wildcard with only Teleport—likely a retreat or repositioning tool, not an offensive threat. With zero healing items, no acquisition allowance, and finite move-change budget (2), Terry must conserve resources aggressively. His behavior—moderate adaptability, strong resource conservation, and signature attachment—implies he’ll favor Charmander as the anchor, using stat boosts to snowball advantage, while Pidgeotto and Rattata apply early pressure or disrupt. Abra may be held in reserve for emergency repositioning. Public evidence hints at past sightings of Bulbasaur and Ivysaur, but relevance is older; no current opponent lead is known. Terry’s confidence borders on dismissiveness—he expects to dominate, but his caution and patience suggest he’ll observe before committing. Uncertainty looms over the unseen player party; any misstep could force him into a reactive, resource-draining stall. His plan: leverage Charmander’s setup potential, use quick attackers to control tempo, and preserve Abra for tactical escape. Victory hinges on maintaining momentum without overextending.
